idiom_name: Map<string, Entity[]> with a typed cell-key helper
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds types, not a spatial index: the manual realization is a Map keyed by cell coordinates with helper functions that keep the key encoding and the cell value type explicit (MDN Map). Typed iteration over the cell array applies the exact predicate, and Map's identity comparison makes a single consistent key encoding essential. For static rectangle data, rbush ships typed definitions and replaces the hand grid; per-frame movers keep the typed grid.
pitfalls: Map compares keys by identity: a number key and its string form are different entries, so the cell encoding must be applied in exactly one helper.
Type annotations do not survive to runtime; nothing prevents mixing key encodings inside a plain string map unless the helper is the only entry point.
The same memory-growth trap as JavaScript: empty cell arrays stay in the map unless pruned.

variants.name: RBush R-tree (typed)
variants.implementation_notes: rbush is usable from TypeScript with generic item types: items carry minX/minY/maxX/maxY, search(bbox) returns intersecting items and load() bulk-builds static sets (rbush README). It replaces the typed grid when objects are rectangles and updates are rarer than searches, for example viewport culling or map data. The generic parameter keeps the payload typed without wrapping the tree.
pitfalls: Removal is by reference unless an equals callback is supplied; a copied item silently stays in the tree.
The bulk load() path is for static data; loading scattered updates into a live tree degrades later searches.
TypeScript cannot check that minX <= maxX, so invalid boxes are accepted and simply never match.
